proved: SchemaField::new succeeds iff the supplied exact name is nonempty and within the caller bound, and success retains the exact field identity and every name byte.

SchemaRequirement::new succeeds iff the supplied field sequence is nonempty, within the configured limit, and strictly ordered by every field-identity byte; success retains the exact direction and field sequence.

SchemaEvidence::new succeeds iff the observed identity sequence is within the configured limit and strictly ordered by every identity byte; success retains the exact binding, direction, and observed sequence.
Successful requirement and evidence construction establishes canonical global identity uniqueness from strict full-byte ordering.

SchemaEvidence::covers returns true iff its stored direction equals the requirement direction and every required field identity occurs in the observed identities. The implementation remains a linear two-cursor scan.
SchemaField, SchemaRequirement, SchemaEvidence, and every RequirementEvidence variant have verified actual Clone implementations preserving complete semantic content.

Empty schema observations, observed supersets, missing middle and terminal required fields, direction mismatch, schema and RequirementEvidence clone equality.
